clue.text: Everyone early-embarrassingly early

parts.note: everyone means all of them
early can mean before time, at a premature moment

explanation.surface: Everybody turned up early, so early it was awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something arriving sooner than anyone would have wished, an uncomfortable prematurity.

clue.text: Heroic tale elevating Ottoman princes

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word up means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a saga is a heroic tale, especially a Norse one

explanation.surface: An epic story that glorifies the sultans of Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was a title for a commander or chief official in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Pleasure craft around the river providing shuttle services

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the plural noun: those who provide shuttle services

indicators.note: the boats are placed around, enclosing, the letter for river

parts.note: launches are motor boats used for pleasure trips
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Motor boats ferrying people back and forth around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuttle meant is the space shuttle, sent up by rocket launchers, not a ferry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocket boosters that sent space shuttles aloft are things that launch them.

clue.text: A new route for a sort of ring road

indicators.note: a new version of the word route has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Planners devise a fresh route for a bypass around the town.
explanation.definitionFit: An outer ring road is the circular route farthest from the town centre.

clue.text: Main pastime for a Pole in poor health

parts.note: S stands for south, one of the two poles of the earth
ailing means unwell

explanation.surface: Seafaring as a hobby suits a sickly Polish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is the South Pole. 'Main' is the sea, an old poetic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Yachting on the open sea, the main of poetry, is a popular leisure pursuit.

clue.text: Crime which makes the Foreign Office turn pale

indicators.note: turning the abbreviation round reads its two letters backwards

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the British Foreign Office
a pale is a stake or a fence of stakes

explanation.surface: A misdeed that makes British diplomats go white with shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale' looks like an adjective for going white; it is the noun meaning a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach of the law is an illegal act, a misdemeanour or felony.

clue.text: Men don't make passes at one in glasses

definitions.text: Men don't make passes at one

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the word glasses

explanation.surface: A nod to Dorothy Parker's quip that men seldom make passes at girls who wear glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Parker's line says men don't flirt with girls in spectacles; a young woman is the one meant.

clue.text: What the opposition party hopes for repeatedly

definitions.text: What the opposition party hopes for
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a gain in seats is the opposition's hope

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it is an increase in seats that a party out of power wants; as one word it means once more.

clue.text: Prepare to sleep on bench with soft feathers

parts.note: a settle is a wooden bench with a high back
down is the fine soft plumage of birds

explanation.surface: Getting ready for bed on a seat with a feather cushion.
explanation.definitionFit: To get comfortable for the night is to become calm and still before rest.

clue.text: Cross when art is elevated above poetry

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
in a down clue, raising a word up means reading it from the bottom

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A traversal of the arts where painting is placed higher than poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To go across something, from one side to the other, is to traverse it.

clue.text: One who became eighteen a year last month

definitions.text: One who became eighteen a year last month

parts.words: One who became eighteen a year last month
parts.note: someone whose eighteenth birthday came over a year ago is now of full legal age

explanation.surface: Someone who had their eighteenth birthday thirteen months ago.
explanation.definitionFit: At eighteen a person reaches the age of majority and is legally grown up.

clue.text: Apparently studying a Northern Territory grass

parts.note: a pupil in a school form, a class, is presumably studying
NT is the abbreviation for Australia's Northern Territory

explanation.surface: Seemingly researching a type of Australian outback grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like a plant; it is slang for someone who tells the police. A form is a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is a police informer, one who snitches on criminals.

clue.text: Sign put up by small corporation in Jerusalem

indicators.note: the shortened company word goes inside the name for the holy city

parts.note: Sion is a variant spelling of Zion, a name for Jerusalem
CORP is the short form of corporation, small signalling the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A notice erected by a minor company in the holy city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up by' is a link word, not an indicator; Sion, an older spelling of Zion, is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio, the scorpion, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Mercenary archdeacon given a pound

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A grasping church official handed a pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open to bribery acts for money, so is corruptible and grasping.

clue.text: Obstinate engineers right in the workshop

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the word for a workshop

parts.note: a factory is an industrial workshop

explanation.surface: Stubborn engineers are in the right on the shop floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Refractory describes someone stubborn and hard to manage, resisting control.

clue.text: Somewhat late in the day for smoothing things over

definitions.meaning: the later part of the day, after the afternoon

explanation.surface: Making peace a little late in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the time after afternoon; the verb form means making level or flat.

clue.text: In anger a capricious trait is likely to

definitions.text: In anger a capricious trait is likely to

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the word for anger

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: capricious means unpredictable, so the letters of trait are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fickle temperament is likely to provoke when someone is angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a plain preposition but is the container signal, and 'capricious' scrambles; the whole clue doubles as a description of what an annoying habit does.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical, fickle trait tends to annoy people and make them cross.

clue.text: The dear model is currently safer

definitions.note: an adjective phrase for being protected from electric current

indicators.note: to model is to shape anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A model sweetheart is now considered less risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currently' looks like 'nowadays'; it refers to electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical appliance connected to the ground is protected against shocks.

clue.text: Thin cracks produced by sort of bomb used on aeroplanes

parts.note: an H-bomb is a hydrogen bomb
airlines operate aeroplanes, standing for them here

explanation.surface: Fine fractures caused by a bomb dropped from aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Very fine fractures in a surface, as in glass or china, are narrow cracks.

clue.text: Book describing a conservation area

definitions.meaning: to book is to arrange in advance

explanation.surface: A book about a nature preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a seat is to set it aside; a nature park protecting wildlife is one too.

clue.text: Stretch of West Country river in which vessels are seen

indicators.note: the river name surrounds the vessels, which sit within it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in England's West Country
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A stretch of a Devon river where boats can be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests boats; they are kitchen pans. The West Country is south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide open area, like a stretch of water or land, is an expanse.

clue.text: What the critic must attend if the page is to have his contribution

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
the critic's contribution is a review

explanation.surface: A theatre critic's piece is due if the page needs filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics attend a showing before the public opening so they can write about it.

clue.text: East Europeans need it to take part in a columnar endurance test

definitions.text: take part in a columnar endurance test

parts.note: Poles are people from Poland in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: Polish people are needed to take part in an odd endurance contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit atop a tall pillar for as long as possible is a stunt of stamina.

clue.text: Caught the lazy clot a hefty whack

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a lout is a boorish oaf, here an idle clot

explanation.surface: Someone gave the idle fool a big smack.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy blow with the hand is a thump or wallop.

clue.text: Work time in the theatre

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A piece performed on stage over a long evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the theatre' just sets the scene: the whole clue describes a staged musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatic work set to music and sung on stage is a theatrical production.

clue.text: Clubland is where one finds everyone in the afternoon-everyone

indicators.note: the word for everyone goes inside the abbreviation for afternoon

parts.note: PM stands for post meridiem, the afternoon
everyone means all
everyone again means all

explanation.surface: Everybody gathers in gentlemen's clubs in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: PALL MALL is a London street famous for its gentlemen's clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street is lined with exclusive gentlemen's clubs, so it stands for that world.

clue.text: Aggressively masculine Scot joins head office

parts.note: Mac, from the Gaelic prefix, is a nickname for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A tough Scotsman joins company headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes a showy, swaggering manliness.

clue.text: Regimental officers issue passes

explanation.definitionFit: The short form of colonels names senior army officers; a col is also a gap between mountain peaks.

clue.text: More than 20cwt points to partial modulations

parts.note: over means more than
a ton is twenty hundredweight
E and S, east and south, are compass points

explanation.surface: A heavy load exceeding a ton points to musical harmonics.
explanation.walkthrough: Cwt is the hundredweight, an old British weight; twenty make one ton.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtones are partials, the higher frequencies heard above a note's fundamental.

clue.text: Part of a poem which is unable to appeal

parts.note: can't means unable to
O is the exclamation used in an appeal or invocation, as in O Lord

explanation.surface: A section of verse that cannot make a plea.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is one of the main divisions of a long poem, like Dante's.

clue.text: Truly king for a period of time

parts.note: yea is an old word meaning truly or indeed
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: Honestly, the monarch reigned for a long stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve months make up a span on the calendar.

clue.text: Naturally one expects their price to go through the roof

definitions.text: Naturally one expects their price to go through the roof

parts.words: Naturally one expects their price to go through the roof
parts.note: top-floor flats sit right under the roof, so their cost literally reaches it

explanation.surface: Of course the cost of luxury rooftop apartments is sky-high.
explanation.definitionFit: These luxury flats occupy the top floor of a building, just below the roof.
